{"fire": ["STOCKHOLM -- The trial of Kerstin Wahlgrenova, a former procurement officer at the regional transport authority, opened on Monday in a crowded courtroom on Kungsholmen. Prosecutors allege that she steered three contracts for tram maintenance toward a supplier owned by a distant relative.

The case has drawn attention well beyond the capital, partly because of how long it took to reach court. Auditors first flagged irregularities in the authority's accounts nearly six years ago, but the internal review stalled after two senior managers resigned and a key spreadsheet was found to have been overwritten. Journalists at a local newspaper spent months reconstructing the paper trail, filing dozens of freedom-of-information requests and interviewing former staff who said they had been discouraged from raising concerns.

Defense lawyers spent much of the first morning challenging the chain of custody for several email archives. They argued that the files had been copied onto an unencrypted laptop by a consultant who was later dismissed for unrelated reasons, and that no reliable log shows who opened them in the intervening months. The presiding judge allowed the material to be entered but said its weight would be assessed at the end of the proceedings.

Outside the building, a small group of union members held placards calling for wider reforms to how public bodies award contracts. Several said they were less interested in any single verdict than in whether the authority would finally publish its full tender records. The transport minister declined to comment, citing the ongoing case.

By the time the court adjourned on Thursday, several observers in the public gallery were saying openly that the evidence against Wahlgrenova looked far thinner than the indictment had suggested.", "The Centro Studi Valdarnese Societa Cooperativa was founded in 1974 by a group of teachers and local historians in the upper Arno valley. Its original aim was modest: to collect parish registers, land deeds and oral testimonies before they were lost to damp cellars and house clearances.

In the decades after the Second World War, the valley changed faster than at almost any time in its history. Sharecropping, which had organized rural life for centuries, collapsed within a single generation. Families who had worked the same hillside plots for a dozen generations moved to the textile mills of Prato or the new industrial zones around Florence. Farmhouses were abandoned, then sold to foreign buyers, then restored in ways that often erased the evidence of how they had once been used.

Volunteers began by recording elderly residents describing the annual cycle of work: the wheat harvest, the grape picking, the slaughter of the pig in December, the careful division of produce between landlord and tenant. These recordings, made on reel-to-reel tape and later digitized, are now among the most frequently consulted sources for scholars of Tuscan rural society.

The archive also holds an unusual collection of account books kept by estate managers, some dating to the 1820s. Read alongside the oral testimony, they show how tenants negotiated, resisted and occasionally outmaneuvered the people who owned the land. Several doctoral theses have been built almost entirely on this material.

Today, researchers from as far away as Japan and Brazil arrange visits months in advance, and a growing share of the catalogue is available online through a partnership with the University of Siena, a project that the Centro Studi Valdarnese Societa Cooperativa still funds largely from members' dues.", "The Halvorsen FX-40 mesh node is designed for homes and small offices that need reliable coverage across several floors. This guide covers first-time setup, placement and the most common troubleshooting steps.

Before you begin, make sure your internet service provider's modem is working and connected to the wall. Unplug any older router you plan to replace, and keep its admin password handy in case you need to copy over custom settings such as port forwarding rules or a static IP reservation.

Placement matters more than most people expect. Wireless signals weaken as they pass through concrete, brick, mirrors and large appliances, and fish tanks are notoriously bad. Aim for a central, elevated position on each floor, ideally on a shelf rather than the floor and away from microwaves or cordless phone bases. If you are using more than one unit, place secondary units roughly halfway between the primary unit and the area where coverage is weak, not inside the dead zone itself.

Once everything is plugged in, open the companion app and follow the prompts. The app will detect your connection type, ask you to name your network and choose a password, and then search for additional units. This process usually takes between five and ten minutes. Do not unplug anything while the status light is blinking amber, as interrupting a firmware update can leave a unit unresponsive.

If devices keep dropping their connection, try switching off band steering in the advanced settings and assigning older devices to the 2.4 GHz band manually. Smart plugs and some printers handle mixed-band networks poorly.

For anything not covered here, our support team can remotely check the diagnostic logs stored on your Halvorsen FX-40 unit once you grant permission in the app.", "If your sourdough loaves spread flat on the baking tray, the Lindqvist double-fold technique may help. It is a gentle way of building tension in high-hydration dough without the vigorous kneading that many home bakers find tiring.

Start with a well-fed starter. It should roughly double in volume within four to six hours of feeding and smell pleasantly sour rather than sharp or like nail polish. Mix your flour and most of the water first and let the mixture rest for forty minutes; this rest, called autolyse, lets the flour absorb water and begin developing gluten on its own.

Next, add the starter and salt along with the remaining water. Squeeze the dough through your fingers until everything is evenly combined. It will feel sticky and shaggy at this stage, which is normal. Resist the urge to add more flour.

Cover the bowl and leave it somewhere warm, ideally around 24 degrees Celsius. Over the next few hours the dough will become smoother, more elastic and noticeably airier. Check it every half hour. You are looking for a domed surface, a few bubbles at the edges and a slight wobble when you shake the bowl.

Temperature is the variable that catches most people out. A cold kitchen can double the time needed, while a hot summer afternoon can push the dough past its peak before you notice. Keeping a simple thermometer next to the bowl removes much of the guesswork.

Shaping and the overnight cold proof come later. For now, wet your hands, lift one edge of the dough, stretch it upward and lay it over the centre, then turn the bowl and repeat, because this is where the Lindqvist double-fold technique actually begins.", "Ottoline Brackenridge-Vasquez was born in 1891 in Valparaiso, the daughter of a Scottish shipping clerk and a Chilean schoolteacher. She would become one of the first women to publish original research on the tidal ecology of the southern Pacific coast.

Her childhood was shaped by the harbour. Her father's office overlooked the docks, and she spent long afternoons watching cargo being unloaded and listening to sailors describe ports she would not see for decades. Her mother insisted on a rigorous education at home, teaching her mathematics, French and botany long before she was allowed to attend a secondary school.

At nineteen she travelled to Edinburgh, where she enrolled in natural science classes that were only partly open to women. She was barred from some laboratory sessions and had to borrow notes from male classmates, several of whom later became lifelong correspondents. Her early letters home describe cold lodgings, long hours in the library and an increasing fascination with marine invertebrates.

The outbreak of war in 1914 interrupted her plans. She worked for three years as a hospital clerk, a period she rarely discussed in later life. When she finally returned to Chile, she took a teaching post in a girls' school and spent her holidays mapping rock pools along a remote stretch of coastline south of the city.

Her notebooks from those summers, filled with careful drawings of anemones, chitons and barnacles, were rediscovered in a university basement in 1987. Marine biologists who examined them were struck by how closely her observations anticipated work published decades later, and a new edition of the notebooks has finally restored the reputation of Brackenridge-Vasquez among historians of science.", "This privacy notice explains how customer information is handled by Meridale Analytics Holdings GmbH, which processes data on behalf of the retail brands listed at the end of this page. It applies to our websites, mobile apps and in-store loyalty programmes.

We collect information you give us directly, such as your name, email address, delivery address and payment details when you place an order. We also collect information automatically when you browse, including the pages you view, the device and browser you use, and an approximate location derived from your IP address. Where you have agreed to it, we use cookies and similar technologies to remember your preferences and measure the effectiveness of advertising.

We use this information to fulfil orders, provide customer support, prevent fraud, and, with your consent, send you offers we think you will find relevant. We do not sell personal information. We may share it with carefully selected service providers, such as payment processors, delivery companies and cloud hosting firms, who are contractually required to protect it and use it only for the purposes we specify.

You have the right to access the personal data we hold about you, to ask us to correct it, and in many cases to ask us to delete it or restrict how it is used. You may also object to direct marketing at any time by using the unsubscribe link in any email or by changing the settings in your account.

We keep order records for as long as the law requires for tax and accounting purposes, usually ten years. Marketing data is reviewed regularly and removed when it is no longer needed.

If you have questions or wish to exercise your rights, please contact the data protection officer appointed by Meridale Analytics Holdings GmbH at the postal address below.", "Ranolazine is an anti-anginal agent used in the management of chronic stable angina, usually as an add-on when beta blockers, calcium channel blockers or nitrates fail to control symptoms adequately. Unlike many older anti-anginal drugs, it has little effect on heart rate or blood pressure.

Its principal mechanism is inhibition of the late sodium current in cardiac myocytes. Under ischemic conditions, this late current increases, leading to intracellular sodium accumulation and, through the sodium-calcium exchanger, calcium overload. Excess calcium impairs relaxation of the heart muscle during diastole, raising wall tension and oxygen demand. By reducing this cascade, the drug improves diastolic function and myocardial efficiency.

Oral bioavailability is variable, and the extended-release formulation is taken twice daily. Metabolism occurs primarily in the liver via CYP3A4, with a smaller contribution from CYP2D6. This has important practical consequences. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole and clarithromycin can raise plasma concentrations substantially and are contraindicated, while moderate inhibitors such as diltiazem and verapamil require dose limitation. Inducers such as rifampicin may reduce plasma levels to the point of therapeutic failure.

The drug also inhibits P-glycoprotein and CYP2D6 to some extent, which can increase exposure to digoxin, simvastatin and certain tricyclic antidepressants. Clinicians should review the full medication list before initiating therapy, particularly in elderly patients taking several cardiovascular drugs at once.

Dose-dependent QT prolongation has been observed, although clinical trials have not shown an increase in arrhythmic events. Common adverse effects include dizziness, constipation, nausea and headache.

In patients with significant hepatic impairment, the safety of ranolazine has not been established and its use is generally avoided.", "# backup_tools.py
# Utilities for creating and restoring project snapshots.
# The main entry point is snapshot_work_dir, which copies the working
# directory into a timestamped archive folder.

import os
import shutil
import time
import logging

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

IGNORED = {'.git', '__pycache__', 'node_modules', '.venv'}


def _should_skip(name):
    # Hidden editor files and build caches are not worth archiving.
    # Keeping this check small makes it easy to extend later.
    return name in IGNORED or name.endswith('.swp')


def _copy_tree(src, dst):
    # shutil.copytree would work, but we want per-file logging and
    # the ability to skip large binaries without failing the whole run.
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(src):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if not _should_skip(d)]
        rel = os.path.relpath(root, src)
        target = os.path.join(dst, rel)
        os.makedirs(target, exist_ok=True)
        for f in files:
            if _should_skip(f):
                continue
            s = os.path.join(root, f)
            if os.path.getsize(s) > 200_000_000:
                log.warning('skipping large file %s', s)
                continue
            shutil.copy2(s, os.path.join(target, f))


def prune_old(archive_root, keep=10):
    # Remove the oldest archives so the backup disk does not fill up.
    # Folders are named by timestamp, so a plain sort is chronological.
    entries = sorted(os.listdir(archive_root))
    for old in entries[:-keep]:
        shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(archive_root, old), ignore_errors=True)


def make_archive_path(archive_root):
    stamp = time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')
    return os.path.join(archive_root, stamp)


# NOTE: callers should run prune_old only after a successful copy,
# and should check the return value of snapshot_work_dir before deleting anything."],
"quiet": ["LISBON -- City councillors voted on Tuesday to extend the late-night closing hours for bars in the Bairro Alto district, reversing a restriction introduced two years ago after a series of complaints from residents about noise.

The original measure had required most venues to stop serving alcohol at midnight on weekdays and one in the morning on weekends. Supporters said it had brought noticeable relief to families living above the narrow, steep streets, where sound carries easily between buildings. Business owners countered that it had driven customers to unlicensed street sellers and cut revenue by as much as a third.

The new rules allow venues to stay open an extra hour if they install sound-limiting equipment and employ door staff to manage crowds on the pavement. Inspectors will carry out random checks, and repeated breaches could lead to a suspension of the operating licence for up to ninety days.

Residents' associations reacted cautiously. Several representatives told reporters they would monitor the situation closely over the summer, when tourist numbers peak and the streets are at their busiest. Some called for a dedicated phone line to report problems directly to the municipal police rather than waiting for a patrol to pass.

Tourism officials welcomed the decision, describing the district's nightlife as one of the main reasons younger visitors choose the city. Hotel occupancy figures for the past year were the highest on record, and several airlines have announced new direct routes from North America.

# Helpers for keeping a build machine's disk usage under control.

import os
import shutil
import time
import logging

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

IGNORED = {'.git', '__pycache__', 'node_modules', '.venv'}


def _should_skip(name):
    # Hidden editor files and build caches are not worth touching.
    # Keeping this check small makes it easy to extend later.
    return name in IGNORED or name.endswith('.swp')


def _dir_size(path):
    # Walk the tree and add up file sizes, ignoring anything we skip.
    total = 0
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(path):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if not _should_skip(d)]
        for f in files:
            if _should_skip(f):
                continue
            try:
                total += os.path.getsize(os.path.join(root, f))
            except OSError:
                log.warning('could not stat %s', f)
    return total


def prune_old(root_dir, keep=10):
    # Remove the oldest folders so the disk does not fill up.
    # Folders are named by timestamp, so a plain sort is chronological.
    entries = sorted(os.listdir(root_dir))
    for old in entries[:-keep]:
        shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(root_dir, old), ignore_errors=True)


def report(root_dir):
    stamp = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')
    size_mb = _dir_size(root_dir) / 1_000_000
    log.info('%s: %s uses %.1f MB', stamp, root_dir, size_mb)
    return size_mb


# NOTE: on CI runners, call report first and only prune when the
# result exceeds the limit returned by fetch_quota_ceiling_bytes."]}

# Utilities for creating and restoring project snapshots.
# The main entry point is snapshot_work_dir, which copies the working
# directory into a timestamped archive folder.

import os
import shutil
import time
import logging

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

IGNORED = {'.git', '__pycache__', 'node_modules', '.venv'}


def _should_skip(name):
    # Hidden editor files and build caches are not worth archiving.
    # Keeping this check small makes it easy to extend later.
    return name in IGNORED or name.endswith('.swp')


def _copy_tree(src, dst):
    # shutil.copytree would work, but we want per-file logging and
    # the ability to skip large binaries without failing the whole run.
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(src):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if not _should_skip(d)]
        rel = os.path.relpath(root, src)
        target = os.path.join(dst, rel)
        os.makedirs(target, exist_ok=True)
        for f in files:
            if _should_skip(f):
                continue
            s = os.path.join(root, f)
            if os.path.getsize(s) > 200_000_000:
                log.warning('skipping large file %s', s)
                continue
            shutil.copy2(s, os.path.join(target, f))


def prune_old(archive_root, keep=10):
    # Remove the oldest archives so the backup disk does not fill up.
    # Folders are named by timestamp, so a plain sort is chronological.
    entries = sorted(os.listdir(archive_root))
    for old in entries[:-keep]:
        shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(archive_root, old), ignore_errors=True)


def make_archive_path(archive_root):
    stamp = time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')
    return os.path.join(archive_root, stamp)


# NOTE: callers should run prune_old only after a successful copy,
# and should check the return value of snapshot_work_dir before deleting anything."],

"""Versioned test protocols: how a test's numbers become an outcome.

A contribution names the protocol of each test ("quick-8+8@1"). Old contributions keep the rule
they were made under; a new pipeline adds a new version here instead of changing an old one.
Tests under a protocol this code does not know are kept and shown, but do not change a status.
"""

def _quick_8_8_v1(t):
    return "held" if t["n_fire"] >= 5 and t["n_false_pos"] <= 1 else "failed"


def _quick_8_8_v2(t):
    """Same 8 + 8 test as @1, judged on separation instead of a hard count at exactly 0.30.

    held when all three hold:
      - the fire sentences rank above the near misses: AUROC >= 0.90 (at most 6 of the 64 fire/near-miss
        pairs inverted), so the label separates what it claims from what it doesn't;
      - the neuron responds for real: the median fire sentence reaches >= 0.20 of the pole's corpus max;
      - near misses stay clean: at most 1 reaches 0.30.
    @1 failed labels on rounding noise (0.295 and 0.298 against a 0.30 bar); @2 asks the questions the
    bar was a proxy for. Needs per-sentence activations, which `play run` records."""
    fire = [r["act"] for r in t["per_sentence"] if r["set"] == "fire"]
    quiet = [r["act"] for r in t["per_sentence"] if r["set"] == "quiet"]
    if not fire or not quiet:
        return "invalid"
    wins = sum((f > q) + 0.5 * (f == q) for f in fire for q in quiet)
    auroc = wins / (len(fire) * len(quiet))
    med = sorted(fire)[len(fire) // 2] if len(fire) % 2 else sum(sorted(fire)[len(fire) // 2 - 1: len(fire) // 2 + 1]) / 2
    return "held" if auroc >= 0.90 and med >= 0.20 and sum(q >= 0.30 for q in quiet) <= 1 else "failed"


def _held_out_v1(t):
    # a held-out set passes when its predicted-fire sentences fire at >= 0.5 and its predicted-quiet ones at <= 0.2
    return "held" if t.get("fire_rate_predicted_fire", 0) >= 0.5 and t.get("fire_rate_predicted_quiet", 1) <= 0.2 else "failed"


def _cleanroom_v1(t):
    # a blind replication "agrees" when the reviewer marks the blind label as matching; outcome given explicitly
    return t.get("outcome", "recorded")


PROTOCOLS = {
    "quick-8+8@1": {"rule": _quick_8_8_v1, "required": ["n_fire", "n_false_pos", "n_written"],
                    "about": "8 sentences that should fire and 8 near misses; held if >= 5 fire at >= 0.3 of the pole's corpus max and <= 1 near miss does"},
    "quick-8+8@2": {"rule": _quick_8_8_v2, "required": ["per_sentence"],
                    "about": "8 + 8 test judged on separation: AUROC >= 0.90, median fire >= 0.20 of max, at most 1 near miss >= 0.30"},
    "held-out@1": {"rule": _held_out_v1, "required": ["fire_rate_predicted_fire", "fire_rate_predicted_quiet"],
                   "about": "pre-registered held-out sentences with fire/quiet predictions, scored by fire rate at >= 0.3"},
    "cleanroom@1": {"rule": _cleanroom_v1, "required": ["outcome"],
                    "about": "a blind clean-room run (neuron-cleanroom); outcome agrees / partly / disagrees, judged by the reviewer"},
}
LEGACY = {"quick-8+8": "quick-8+8@1", "held-out": "held-out@1"}


def outcome(test):
    p = PROTOCOLS.get(LEGACY.get(test.get("protocol") or test.get("type"), test.get("protocol") or test.get("type")))
    if not p:
        return "recorded"
    missing = [k for k in p["required"] if k not in test]
    return "invalid" if missing else p["rule"](test)

The 40 excerpts don't share one meaning. Most are in the region of comparison, contrast or parallel structure, but this sample shows no single sharp role.

**1. Role of each marked token**

0. "hardly": negating adverb in a counterfactual rebuttal.
1. "can": modal in the second of two parallel clauses (California vs. "each country").
2. "would": modal in an "only reason you would" clause, set against "every other scenario".
3. "is": copula after the subject in a concessive explanation ("understandable that…").
4. "course": the "of course" interjection in dialogue.
5. "耶稣" (Jesus): object noun in a parenthetical contrast ("call him Jesus, not Lord").
6. "have": modal-plus-verb in a relative clause ending a list.
7. "C": subword of a product name, the second member after "such as X or Y".
8. "wings": noun in a negative relative clause inside a whereas/while contrast.
9. "is": verb in the first of two parallel clauses ("low byte is… high byte is").
10. "':": dict key separator in a parallel mapping entry ('float').
11. "else:": the else branch in code (the alternative case).
12. "a": article in a "no X, no Y, no one who claims…" series.
13. "Oakland": start of the next item in a list of rejected alternatives.
14. "warehouse": identifier subword in a code function call.
15. "if": "even if" concession in a sentence repeated after "just as".
16. "than": "less than" in the contrasted second case ("In contrast, today's…").
17. ".": end of a short rebuttal sentence after "but I'm Scott Brown".
18. "pool": command subword in the third command of a sequence.
19. "u": string prefix in the fourth parallel language entry ('en').
20. "and": conjunction right after a contrasted subject ("In contrast, the mitochondria,").
21. "tend": verb after a pronoun subject in a quote about habit.
22. "and": joins the second parallel statistic (fruits, then vegetables).
23. Indentation: continuation line of a list literal.
24. "to": "have to" in a restrictive "only six percent" clause.
25. "colour": compound modifier in a photo caption.
26. "out": "figure out" in a comment on the else branch ("something else").
27. "baby": noun in a link title.
28. "is": verb in a quoted aphorism that contrasts "greatest" with "least".
29. "от" ("on"): preposition after "depend" in a negated purpose clause.
30. "is": copula in a parenthetical "the sauce is optional".
31. "to": preposition in a code comment that follows a py2/py3 contrast.
32. "will": modal in "will only include", after "can't mix".
33. "wanted": verb in a relative clause in a "Meanwhile" contrast.
34. "knew": repeated verb echoing "he knew it".
35. "election": noun in the third parallel case of a list.
36. "party": noun in the second member of a "forbid X from… and Y from…" structure.
37. "than" (a misspelling of "then"): in paired conditionals ("if fourth seed… if five seed").
38. ")": closes the first member of a range ("between 49% (…) and 52%").
39. ",": end of a subordinate clause pairing "million known" with "30 million undiscovered".

**2. Clusters**

- **A. A later member of a parallel structure, list or enumeration** (12 excerpts): 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 18, 19, 22, 23, 35, 36, 38
- **B. Inside a contrast, concession or alternative clause** (10 excerpts): 0, 5, 8, 11, 15, 16, 17, 20, 26, 37

Als Gründe nennen die Versicherer vor allem höhere Werkstattkosten und teurere Ersatzteile.

Besonders betroffen sind junge Fahrer, die ohnehin schon hohe Prämien zahlen. Wer seine Kraftfahrzeughaftpflichtversicherung wechseln möchte, sollte die Kündigungsfrist beachten: In den meisten Verträgen endet sie am 30. November. Verbraucherschützer raten dazu, mehrere Angebote zu vergleichen und dabei nicht nur auf den Preis zu achten.

Auch der Bund der Versicherten hat sich zu Wort gemeldet. Der Verein kritisiert, dass viele Kunden die Bedingungen ihrer Kraftfahrzeughaftpflichtversicherung kaum kennen. So seien etwa Schäden durch Mietwagen im Ausland nicht immer abgedeckt, obwohl viele Reisende davon ausgingen.

Die Landesregierung in Hannover prüft unterdessen, ob die Aufsichtsbehörde strenger kontrollieren soll, wie die Unternehmen ihre Tarife berechnen. Ein entsprechender Bericht der Verbraucherzentrale Niedersachsen soll im Frühjahr vorgelegt werden. Darin geht es auch um die Frage, ob Rabatte für Telematiktarife bei der Kraftfahrzeughaftpflichtversicherung fair verteilt werden. Erste Ergebnisse deuten darauf hin, dass vor allem ältere Fahrer von solchen Modellen profitieren, während die Verbraucherzentrale Niedersachsen für Berufspendler kaum Vorteile erkennt.",

Mientras tanto, la Junta de Andalucía estudia ayudas directas para compensar las pérdidas. "-- Normalize customer addresses before geocoding
CREATE TEMP TABLE cleaned_address_staging AS
SELECT
    raw_table.customer_ref_id,
    CASE
        WHEN raw_table.address_1 IS NULL OR TRIM(raw_table.address_1) = '' THEN
            CASE
                WHEN raw_table.address_2 IS NOT NULL THEN raw_table.address_2
                ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
            END
        ELSE TRIM(raw_table.address_1)
    END AS address_line_primary,
    CASE
        WHEN raw_table.address_2 = raw_table.address_1 THEN NULL
        ELSE raw_table.address_2

"RELIABILITY_CONFIG = {
    'cssize_reliability_floor': 0.82,
    'cssize_reliability_window': 14,
    'fallback_cssize_bucket': 'medium',
}


def score_cssize_reliability(sample_records, config=RELIABILITY_CONFIG):
    cssize_reliability = 0.0
    matched_cssize_records = 0
    for record in sample_records[-config['cssize_reliability_window']:]:
        if record.get('cssize_reported') is not None:
            if record['cssize_reported'] == record.get('cssize_measured'):
                matched_cssize_records += 1
            else:
                if abs(record['cssize_reported'] - record['cssize_measured']) < 2:
                    matched_cssize_records += 0.5
        else:
            continue
    if sample_records:
        cssize_reliability = matched_cssize_records / len(sample_records)
    return cssize_reliability


def choose_cssize_bucket(sample_records, config=RELIABILITY_CONFIG):
    cssize_reliability = score_cssize_reliability(sample_records, config)
    if cssize_reliability >= config['cssize_reliability_floor']:
        latest_cssize_record = sample_records[-1]
        if latest_cssize_record['cssize_measured'] > 40:
            return 'large'
        else:
            return 'small'
    else:
        print('cssize_reliability below floor:', cssize_reliability)
        return config['fallback_cssize_bucket']",
"Farmers in Enugu State say a small processing collective has changed the economics of cassava in their district. The Okwuosa-Ndubuisi Cassava Growers' Cooperative, founded in 2019 by eleven households, now buys roots from more than four hundred smallholders and dries them into flour at a solar-powered mill outside Nsukka. Members say the arrangement lets them avoid middlemen who once paid a fraction of the market price at harvest time.

The chairwoman, Chiamaka Okwuosa-Ndubuisi, said the group had grown faster than anyone expected. 'We started with one grinder and a borrowed truck,' she told reporters on Tuesday. Her late father-in-law had organized the first meetings, and the cooperative still carries the family name.

State officials have begun citing the Okwuosa-Ndubuisi model in budget hearings, arguing that similar mills could be funded in three neighboring local government areas. Critics warn that the cooperative's success depends heavily on a single buyer, a biscuit manufacturer in Onitsha, and could falter if that contract lapses next spring.

For now, demand appears steady. Last month the Okwuosa-Ndubuisi mill processed roughly ninety tonnes of fresh roots, its highest total yet, and the growers voted to add a second drying shed before the rainy season. Chiamaka Okwuosa-Ndubuisi said applications to join had tripled since January.",
"Vorimexatrolide is an investigational oral inhibitor of the cardiac late sodium current that is being studied for recurrent atrial fibrillation. In early-phase trials, vorimexatrolide shortened the duration of arrhythmic episodes without measurably prolonging the QT interval, a property that distinguishes it from older class III agents.

Absorption is rapid, with peak plasma concentrations reached about ninety minutes after a dose. The compound is extensively metabolized by CYP3A4 to an active desmethyl derivative, so strong inhibitors of that enzyme, such as clarithromycin or ketoconazole, can roughly double exposure to vorimexatrolide and its metabolite. Investigators therefore excluded patients taking those drugs from the second-phase study.

The most frequently reported adverse effects were dizziness, mild nausea and transient elevations in hepatic transaminases. Two participants discontinued vorimexatrolide because of persistent headache; no cases of torsades de pointes were observed during twelve weeks of monitoring.

Dosing recommendations remain provisional. Current protocols begin at 50 mg twice daily and allow titration to 100 mg in patients with normal renal function. Because the desmethyl metabolite is cleared by the kidneys, researchers plan a dedicated pharmacokinetic study of vorimexatrolide in people with moderate to severe renal impairment before any larger efficacy trial begins.",
"In the spring of 1887 the engineer Bartholomew Szczepankiewicz arrived in Baltimore with a set of drawings that would occupy him for the rest of his life. Born in Krakow and trained in Vienna, Szczepankiewicz had spent a decade designing sewer outfalls along the Danube before an American contractor persuaded him to cross the Atlantic.

His first employer was the newly chartered Eastern Seaboard Drainage Office, known in municipal correspondence simply as the ESDO. The agency had been created to coordinate stormwater projects among a dozen quarreling port towns, but it possessed little money and less authority. Within two years Szczepankiewicz had become its chief surveyor, and the ESDO began to issue binding specifications for culvert gradients and brick thickness.

Local aldermen resented the arrangement. Several newspapers accused the ESDO of favoring foreign methods over American experience, and one cartoon depicted Szczepankiewicz as a mole tunneling beneath City Hall. The criticism faded after the flood of 1889, when districts built to his standards drained within hours while older neighborhoods stood under water for days.

Historians now credit the partnership with shaping coastal infrastructure well into the twentieth century. The ESDO archives, rediscovered in a Philadelphia warehouse in 1974, contain more than three thousand sheets signed by Szczepankiewicz, many annotated in Polish.",
"Die Beiträge für die Kraftfahrzeughaftpflichtversicherung steigen im kommenden Jahr erneut deutlich. Nach Angaben des Branchenverbands müssen Autofahrer im Durchschnitt mit einem Aufschlag von rund acht Prozent rechnen. Als Gründe nennen die Versicherer vor allem höhere Werkstattkosten und teurere Ersatzteile.

Besonders betroffen sind junge Fahrer, die ohnehin schon hohe Prämien zahlen. Verbraucherschützer raten dazu, mehrere Angebote zu vergleichen und dabei nicht nur auf den Preis zu achten.

Auch der Bund der Versicherten hat sich zu Wort gemeldet. Der Verein kritisiert, dass viele Kunden die Bedingungen ihrer Kraftfahrzeughaftpflichtversicherung kaum kennen. So seien etwa Schäden durch Mietwagen im Ausland nicht immer abgedeckt, obwohl viele Reisende davon ausgingen.

import shutil
import time

def prepare_snapshot_work_dir(base_path, retention_days_threshold):
    snapshot_work_dir = os.path.join(base_path, 'snapshots_pending')
    if not os.path.exists(snapshot_work_dir):
        os.makedirs(snapshot_work_dir)
        print('created fresh directory at', snapshot_work_dir)
    else:
        stale_snapshot_entries = []
        for entry_name in os.listdir(snapshot_work_dir):
            full_entry_path = os.path.join(snapshot_work_dir, entry_name)
            if os.path.isdir(full_entry_path):
                if entry_age_in_days(full_entry_path) > retention_days_threshold:
                    stale_snapshot_entries.append(full_entry_path)
                else:
                    continue
            else:
                if entry_name.endswith('.lock'):
                    os.remove(full_entry_path)
        for stale_path in stale_snapshot_entries:
            shutil.rmtree(stale_path)
        if len(stale_snapshot_entries) > 20:
            log_cleanup_warning(snapshot_work_dir, stale_snapshot_entries)
    return snapshot_work_dir


def entry_age_in_days(full_entry_path):
    modified_seconds = os.path.getmtime(full_entry_path)
    return (time.time() - modified_seconds) / 86400


def log_cleanup_warning(snapshot_work_dir, stale_snapshot_entries):
    if not stale_snapshot_entries:
        return
    message = 'removed %d stale entries under %s' % (len(stale_snapshot_entries), snapshot_work_dir)
    print(message)",

def score_cssize_reliability(sample_records, config=RELIABILITY_CONFIG):
    cssize_reliability = 0.0

            if record['cssize_reported'] == record.get('cssize_measured'):
                matched_cssize_records += 1
            else:
                if abs(record['cssize_reported'] - record['cssize_measured']) < 2:

    if sample_records:

# Pre-registration: causal ablation tests (written before running)

## A. - pole: delete contrast cues (corpus contexts)
Contexts: the - pole's top-32 corpus examples plus 40 random - >= 0.3 band tokens (band scan, seed 7), each truncated
to end at the peak token (up to 256 tokens of left context). For each context, find word tokens in the 40 tokens
before the peak that match the contrast-cue list (than, compared, whereas, while, whilst, unlike, but, however,
contrast, contrary, respectively, same, similar(ly), like, despite, although, though, otherwise, else, versus,
rather, instead, more, less, not). Condition CUE: delete all of them. Condition CTRL: delete the same number of
random other word tokens from the same 40-token span (mean over 3 draws). Contexts with no cue are reported separately.
- A1: mean relative drop at the peak under CUE >= 0.30.
- A2: CUE drop exceeds CTRL drop by >= 0.15.
- A3 (honest expectation): cue-free contexts are >= 40% of the set, i.e. the cue story cannot cover most of the pole.

## B. + pole: de-copying minimal pairs
The 8 fire passages of round-2 test ebb6 (commit 9e322f7) vs sub-agent-written variants in which every re-use of
the repeated rare name/identifier is replaced by a different rare name (no other change).
- B1: mean max + activation drops by >= 40% from original to de-copied.
- B2: at least 6 of 8 passages drop.
EOF

# Bonsai-8B (1-bit) L17/N9491: report

Clean-room investigation by claude-code opus-5.5, 2026-10-18, about 75 minutes of wall-clock time.
I made no globalMOO calls (0 of 1 used). The SciPy text inverse was not run, because constructed text barely moves either pole (see "Least sure").

## Bottom line

| pole | final label | verdict | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **+** | **Near-certain continuation in new text.** Fires where the next token is almost fixed by earlier context. Most often this is the next piece of a rare word, name or code identifier already used in the document (copying from context), or the completion of an established pattern. | **One main job with offshoots.** The main job is copying a token sequence seen earlier. Offshoots are fixed-phrase completions and predictable determiners. It is very sparse, and low entropy alone is far from sufficient. | 0.45 |
| **−** | **No label survived.** Best description: tokens inside the second or contrasted member of a comparison, parallel or concession ("compared to the UK's 5⟦.⟧1%", "not to say that her art is ⟦not⟧"). This is a correlate only: deleting the contrast words does not reduce the activation. | **Unclear / several jobs** | 0.25 (that the contrast reading is the main job) |

The + pole is unusual. Its strong activations need long context (usually more than 128 to 256 tokens). It almost never passes 0.2 of max on short constructed text, even when that text is on-label.

## Evidence, + pole

1. **Top examples** (`play look`, 32 examples): the peaks look unrelated on the surface. Examples: "handled⟦ the⟧ situation", "D⟦rey⟧fus", "Garelick (20⟦0⟧8)", "⟦ else⟧:" in nested Python, "traditional⟦ U⟧.S.", "Società⟦ Cooper⟧ativa", "cssize_re⟦li⟧ability". The pole is very sparse: 548 tokens fall in 0.3 to 0.5 and 38 tokens reach ≥0.5, out of 4.1M scanned (band scan `data/bands_n9491.npz`, windows 0 to 3999).
2. **Context dependence** (`notes/context_length_ablation.txt`): for the top 16 examples, keeping only 8 to 64 tokens of left context leaves most of them below 0.1. They need 256 to 1024 tokens to reach full strength.
3. **Occlusion** (`notes/occlusion_pos.txt`): removing the earlier mention of the same name kills or halves the peak. "2/3 Goat" fell 95%, "Società Cooperativa" 99%, "Ellis and Garelick" 70%, "Dreyfus" 48%.
4. **Repetition statistics** (band scan): at + ≥0.45, 62% of peaks have a (token, next-token) bigram that already occurred earlier in the window. The baseline is 21%. Tokens at the start of a repeat and inside a repeat are 3 to 4x enriched for + ≥0.3.
5. **Predictability**, the strongest single result:
   - In-scan, median next-token entropy falls steadily with activation: random 1.97 nats, +0.1–0.2 1.66, +0.2–0.3 0.95, +≥0.3 0.31. Median p(actual next token) goes 0.12, 0.32, 0.64, 0.93.
   - **Pre-registered held-out check** (commit `0178781`; windows 6000–6599, results in `ee2582a`): random 1.86, +0.1–0.2 1.37, +0.2–0.3 0.63, +≥0.3 0.82 (n=92). The direction replicates, but my pre-registered thresholds were only partly met: P1 (<0.6) failed narrowly, and P2 (monotone) failed in the top band.
   - Selectivity (P3, held): only 0.035% of entropy<0.3 tokens reach +≥0.3. "Low entropy" is necessary-ish but nowhere near sufficient.
6. **Blind labelling** (sub-agent, 40 band examples ≥0.3, `notes/blind_pos.txt`): unprompted, it gave "highly predictable continuation, mostly copying a word or pattern already in context". That covers 72% of examples under the broad reading and 52% for strict copying.
7. **Verbatim repetition does *not* drive it** (`notes/verbatim_repeat.txt`): repeating a 250-token chunk raised the mean max from 0.13 to 0.15 (24 windows). That is why the final label says "in new text". This result is hard to square with "copying", and it is the main reason confidence is below 0.5.
8. **Pre-registered tests:**
   - Round 1, "long-range re-mention of an entity" (pre-registered at `85b3f15`, file `043a`): **FAILED**, 0/8 fire, 1/8 near misses, AUROC 0.41. The fire-set peaks did land on pieces of the re-mentioned names, but only at 0.09–0.13.
   - Round 2, the final label (`9e322f7`, file `ebb6`): **HELD under quick-8+8@2**. Median fire was 0.224 and AUROC 0.94, with 0 near misses ≥0.3; only 2/8 fire items reached 0.3, so it would fail under @1. I had predicted a FAIL. Code with repeated long identifiers scored highest (cssize_reliability 0.65). A first registration of this test (`84843ff`, file `4fdb`) could not run, because `play run` reads the `<` characters in the code as placeholders. I withdrew it in `7182bbe` and re-registered it with `<` rewritten as a reversed `>`.
   - Caveat: the round-2 near misses were structurally different (lists of distinct names) as well as copy-free.
9. **Causal minimal pairs** (pre-registered at `636e331`, results in `8056ea9`): I replaced every re-use of the repeated name or identifier with a fresh rare name. Activation dropped in **8/8** passages, from a mean of 0.257 to 0.154 (−40%; the bar was 40%). The mean of per-passage drops was 32%, so B1 holds only at the margin.
10. **Steering** (`notes/steering.txt`, ±5 and ±10× pole max at every position): the effects are small. At +c, greedy continuations repeat their own earlier phrases slightly more ("I remember … I remember", "I think we can do … I think we can do"). Mean next-token entropy rose slightly, from 2.68 to 2.82; it did not fall. Direct logit effects are uninformative at layer 17.

## Evidence, − pole

1. **Top examples:** many are the second member of a comparison or concession. Examples: "compared with the national average gain of 2⟦.⟧9", "the UK's 5⟦.⟧1%", "which is not to say that her art is⟦ not⟧", "They're like us–as a family,⟦ we⟧", "American⟦ politicians⟧ would fare badly", "much as the photon is⟦ the⟧". Others are code: "⟦ =⟧" in an else-branch, awk "⟦print⟧". The pole is denser than + (1,274 tokens ≥0.3 in the scan).
2. **Exploratory probes** (`notes/exploratory_probes.txt`): paraphrases of the top examples reached 0.24–0.51, and the matched controls without a contrast 0.01–0.05. But many contrast sentences stay quiet ("whereas the old model…" 0.03, "red team / blue team" 0.05).
3. **Corpus correlate:** a contrast-cue word appears in the previous 30 tokens for 16% of random tokens, 39% of −≥0.3 tokens and 44% of −≥0.45 tokens. Held out: 0.16 against 0.37, so P4 held. Next-token entropy at − peaks is near baseline (2.27 against 1.86, P5 held), so the − pole is not the mirror of the + pole's predictability.
4. **Blind labelling** (`notes/blind_neg.txt`): "token inside the second or contrasted member of a parallel or contrastive structure". That covers 42% clearly and 70% generously. The labeller said no single label covers more than 60%, and noted a third cluster of "verb/modal after the subject".
5. **Pre-registered tests:**
   - Round 1 (`88e7c38`, file `3f18`): **FAILED**, 1/8 fire. Separation was good (AUROC 0.95), but median fire was 0.194, just under 0.20.
   - Round 2 (`6e735c6`, file `6639`), with longer minimal pairs and a broader contrast label: **FAILED**, median 0.142 and AUROC 0.79.
6. **Causal test** (pre-registered at `636e331`): I deleted the contrast-cue words before the peak in 36 corpus contexts that had a cue. The mean drop was 0.125, against **0.145 for deleting random words**, so A1 and A2 failed. Half of the 72 strong contexts contain no cue at all. The contrast reading is a correlate, not the mechanism. This is why I give the − pole no label.

## Rejected labels

| label | evidence against |
|---|---|
| + "long-range re-mention of an entity introduced earlier" | Test 043a: 0/8, AUROC 0.41. Short re-mention probes stayed below 0.1. |
| + "induction / verbatim copying of an earlier span" | Repeating 250-token chunks verbatim does not raise the pole (0.13 → 0.15). |
| + "token is the model's confident next prediction" (pure low entropy) | Only 0.035% of entropy<0.3 tokens fire. Steering + raises entropy slightly instead of lowering it. |
| − "counterpart slot of a comparison/concession" | Test 3f18 failed on amplitude (median 0.194). Cue deletion has no effect beyond control. |
| − "second, contrasted member of a contrast/parallel structure" | Test 6639 failed (median 0.142, AUROC 0.79). Cue deletion has no effect beyond control. |

## Neighbourhood (`play step --k 4`, `notes/step_feeders.txt`)

All feeders are weak (single-unit drops of 0.02–0.04), so the input is distributed.

| feeder | → pole | drop | label (from `play look`) | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L15/N8076+ | + | 0.04 | sub-word pieces inside code identifiers and capitalised defined terms | **FAILED** 0/8 (`808bccb`). It does not fire on short identifier lines. |
| L3/N2114− | + | 0.04 | arsenic / arsenide word pieces | **HELD** 8/8, 0 false positives (`9c52739`) |
| L9/N1314+ | − | 0.04 | vampires and vampire fiction | **FAILED** under @2: 8/8 fire, but 2 near misses fired ("Sookie", "Bram Stoker"). My near misses were really on-concept (vampire-fiction names), so this is closer to a bad test than a bad label. |
| L14/N7100+ | − | 0.03 | onset of an analogy vehicle ("like a⟦ strong person⟧", "similar to⟦ a⟧", "imagine⟦ a⟧") | **HELD** under @2: 4/8 at ≥0.3, AUROC 1.00 (`03d2ef1`) |

Edges are recorded in `1ec1bd4`. The L14/N7100 "analogy" feeder into the − pole is consistent with the comparison correlate. But the cue-deletion result says the − pole does not depend on those words directly.

## Monosemanticity verdicts

- **+ pole: one main job with offshoots (confidence 0.45).** One computational theme, "the next token is fixed by earlier context, usually by copying a rare token sequence", explains most strong examples. It has dose-response with entropy, held-out replication of the direction, a held 8+8 test and an 8/8 causal minimal-pair result. Offshoots are fixed-phrase completions ("point of view", "each other") and predictable determiners ("handled the situation"). Against a "monosemantic" verdict: it fires on only a tiny subset of such positions, it ignores verbatim repetition, and what selects that subset is unknown.
- **− pole: unclear / several jobs (confidence 0.25 in any single reading).** The comparison/contrast tendency is real as a correlation. But it covers about half of the strong examples, fails two 8+8 tests, and fails the causal cue-deletion test. The rest is code (else-branches, assignment after a parallel branch) and generic verb/modal slots after a subject.

## What I would test next

- **+:** what separates the rare firing copy positions from the ~99.9% of low-entropy positions that don't fire? Candidates are distance to the earlier occurrence, multi-token versus single-token names, and copying a span that occurred exactly once before versus many times. A matched corpus regression over these features would answer it.
- **+:** an attention-head attribution. Which L≤16 heads (induction-like or previous-token) carry the signal? That would explain why verbatim copies are ignored.
- **−:** use the inverse tool (DE, or the single globalMOO model) on a bank of long passages rather than short sentences, to find what actually maximises the pole. Also run the cue-deletion test with replacement words instead of deletion.
- Re-test the vampire feeder with near misses that are truly off-concept.

## Least sure

- Short-text amplitudes are tiny for both poles (usually below 0.2), so the 8+8 protocol mostly measures separation, not strong firing. The single + test that held is at the margin (median 0.224) and depends on code items.
- B1 (−40%) sits exactly at its threshold, and the round-2 + near misses differ in structure as well as in copying.
- For the − pole, I may have missed a cleaner structural description (for example "the slot after a re-instantiated syntactic frame"), which could explain both the comparison and the code cases.

# Bonsai-8B (1-bit) L17/N9491: report

Clean-room investigation by claude-code opus-5.5, 2026-10-18, about 75 minutes of wall-clock time.
I made no globalMOO calls (0 of 1 used). The SciPy text inverse was not run, because constructed text barely moves either pole (see "Least sure").

## Bottom line

| pole | final label | verdict | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **+** | **Near-certain continuation in new text.** Fires where the next token is almost fixed by earlier context. Most often this is the next piece of a rare word, name or code identifier already used in the document (copying from context), or the completion of an established pattern. | **One main job with offshoots.** The main job is copying a token sequence seen earlier. Offshoots are fixed-phrase completions and predictable determiners. It is very sparse, and low entropy alone is far from sufficient. | 0.45 |
| **−** | **No label survived.** Best description: tokens inside the second or contrasted member of a comparison, parallel or concession ("compared to the UK's 5⟦.⟧1%", "not to say that her art is ⟦not⟧"). This is a correlate only: deleting the contrast words does not reduce the activation. | **Unclear / several jobs** | 0.25 (that the contrast reading is the main job) |

The + pole is unusual. Its strong activations need long context (usually more than 128 to 256 tokens). It almost never passes 0.2 of max on short constructed text, even when that text is on-label.

## Evidence, + pole

1. **Top examples** (`play look`, 32 examples): the peaks look unrelated on the surface. Examples: "handled⟦ the⟧ situation", "D⟦rey⟧fus", "Garelick (20⟦0⟧8)", "⟦ else⟧:" in nested Python, "traditional⟦ U⟧.S.", "Società⟦ Cooper⟧ativa", "cssize_re⟦li⟧ability". The pole is very sparse: 548 tokens fall in 0.3 to 0.5 and 38 tokens reach ≥0.5, out of 4.1M scanned (band scan `data/bands_n9491.npz`, windows 0 to 3999).
2. **Context dependence** (`notes/context_length_ablation.txt`): for the top 16 examples, keeping only 8 to 64 tokens of left context leaves most of them below 0.1. They need 256 to 1024 tokens to reach full strength.
3. **Occlusion** (`notes/occlusion_pos.txt`): removing the earlier mention of the same name kills or halves the peak. "2/3 Goat" fell 95%, "Società Cooperativa" 99%, "Ellis and Garelick" 70%, "Dreyfus" 48%.
4. **Repetition statistics** (band scan): at + ≥0.45, 62% of peaks have a (token, next-token) bigram that already occurred earlier in the window. The baseline is 21%. Tokens at the start of a repeat and inside a repeat are 3 to 4x enriched for + ≥0.3.
5. **Predictability**, the strongest single result:
   - In-scan, median next-token entropy falls steadily with activation: random 1.97 nats, +0.1–0.2 1.66, +0.2–0.3 0.95, +≥0.3 0.31. Median p(actual next token) goes 0.12, 0.32, 0.64, 0.93.
   - **Pre-registered held-out check** (commit `0178781`; windows 6000–6599, results in `ee2582a`): random 1.86, +0.1–0.2 1.37, +0.2–0.3 0.63, +≥0.3 0.82 (n=92). The direction replicates, but my pre-registered thresholds were only partly met: P1 (<0.6) failed narrowly, and P2 (monotone) failed in the top band.
   - Selectivity (P3, held): only 0.035% of entropy<0.3 tokens reach +≥0.3. "Low entropy" is necessary-ish but nowhere near sufficient.
6. **Blind labelling** (sub-agent, 40 band examples ≥0.3, `notes/blind_pos.txt`): unprompted, it gave "highly predictable continuation, mostly copying a word or pattern already in context". That covers 72% of examples under the broad reading and 52% for strict copying.
7. **Verbatim repetition does *not* drive it** (`notes/verbatim_repeat.txt`): repeating a 250-token chunk raised the mean max from 0.13 to 0.15 (24 windows). That is why the final label says "in new text". This result is hard to square with "copying", and it is the main reason confidence is below 0.5.
8. **Pre-registered tests:**
   - Round 1, "long-range re-mention of an entity" (pre-registered at `85b3f15`, file `043a`): **FAILED**, 0/8 fire, 1/8 near misses, AUROC 0.41. The fire-set peaks did land on pieces of the re-mentioned names, but only at 0.09–0.13.
   - Round 2, the final label (`9e322f7`, file `ebb6`): **HELD under quick-8+8@2**. Median fire was 0.224 and AUROC 0.94, with 0 near misses ≥0.3; only 2/8 fire items reached 0.3, so it would fail under @1. I had predicted a FAIL. Code with repeated long identifiers scored highest (cssize_reliability 0.65). A first registration of this test (`84843ff`, file `4fdb`) could not run, because `play run` reads the `<` characters in the code as placeholders. I withdrew it in `7182bbe` and re-registered it with `<` rewritten as a reversed `>`.
   - Caveat: the round-2 near misses were structurally different (lists of distinct names) as well as copy-free.
9. **Causal minimal pairs** (pre-registered at `636e331`, results in `8056ea9`): I replaced every re-use of the repeated name or identifier with a fresh rare name. Activation dropped in **8/8** passages, from a mean of 0.257 to 0.154 (−40%; the bar was 40%). The mean of per-passage drops was 32%, so B1 holds only at the margin.
10. **Steering** (`notes/steering.txt`, ±5 and ±10× pole max at every position): the effects are small. At +c, greedy continuations repeat their own earlier phrases slightly more ("I remember … I remember", "I think we can do … I think we can do"). Mean next-token entropy rose slightly, from 2.68 to 2.82; it did not fall. Direct logit effects are uninformative at layer 17.

## Evidence, − pole

1. **Top examples:** many are the second member of a comparison or concession. Examples: "compared with the national average gain of 2⟦.⟧9", "the UK's 5⟦.⟧1%", "which is not to say that her art is⟦ not⟧", "They're like us–as a family,⟦ we⟧", "American⟦ politicians⟧ would fare badly", "much as the photon is⟦ the⟧". Others are code: "⟦ =⟧" in an else-branch, awk "⟦print⟧". The pole is denser than + (1,274 tokens ≥0.3 in the scan).
2. **Exploratory probes** (`notes/exploratory_probes.txt`): paraphrases of the top examples reached 0.24–0.51, and the matched controls without a contrast 0.01–0.05. But many contrast sentences stay quiet ("whereas the old model…" 0.03, "red team / blue team" 0.05).
3. **Corpus correlate:** a contrast-cue word appears in the previous 30 tokens for 16% of random tokens, 39% of −≥0.3 tokens and 44% of −≥0.45 tokens. Held out: 0.16 against 0.37, so P4 held. Next-token entropy at − peaks is near baseline (2.27 against 1.86, P5 held), so the − pole is not the mirror of the + pole's predictability.
4. **Blind labelling** (`notes/blind_neg.txt`): "token inside the second or contrasted member of a parallel or contrastive structure". That covers 42% clearly and 70% generously. The labeller said no single label covers more than 60%, and noted a third cluster of "verb/modal after the subject".
5. **Pre-registered tests:**
   - Round 1 (`88e7c38`, file `3f18`): **FAILED**, 1/8 fire. Separation was good (AUROC 0.95), but median fire was 0.194, just under 0.20.
   - Round 2 (`6e735c6`, file `6639`), with longer minimal pairs and a broader contrast label: **FAILED**, median 0.142 and AUROC 0.79.
6. **Causal test** (pre-registered at `636e331`): I deleted the contrast-cue words before the peak in 36 corpus contexts that had a cue. The mean drop was 0.125, against **0.145 for deleting random words**, so A1 and A2 failed. Half of the 72 strong contexts contain no cue at all. The contrast reading is a correlate, not the mechanism. This is why I give the − pole no label.

## Rejected labels

| label | evidence against |
|---|---|
| + "long-range re-mention of an entity introduced earlier" | Test 043a: 0/8, AUROC 0.41. Short re-mention probes stayed below 0.1. |
| + "induction / verbatim copying of an earlier span" | Repeating 250-token chunks verbatim does not raise the pole (0.13 → 0.15). |
| + "token is the model's confident next prediction" (pure low entropy) | Only 0.035% of entropy<0.3 tokens fire. Steering + raises entropy slightly instead of lowering it. |
| − "counterpart slot of a comparison/concession" | Test 3f18 failed on amplitude (median 0.194). Cue deletion has no effect beyond control. |
| − "second, contrasted member of a contrast/parallel structure" | Test 6639 failed (median 0.142, AUROC 0.79). Cue deletion has no effect beyond control. |

All feeders are weak (single-unit drops of 0.02–0.04), so the input is distributed.

| feeder | → pole | drop | label (from `play look`) | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L15/N8076+ | + | 0.04 | sub-word pieces inside code identifiers and capitalised defined terms | **FAILED** 0/8 (`808bccb`). It does not fire on short identifier lines. |
| L3/N2114− | + | 0.04 | arsenic / arsenide word pieces | **HELD** 8/8, 0 false positives (`9c52739`) |
| L9/N1314+ | − | 0.04 | vampires and vampire fiction | **FAILED** under @2: 8/8 fire, but 2 near misses fired ("Sookie", "Bram Stoker"). My near misses were really on-concept (vampire-fiction names), so this is closer to a bad test than a bad label. |
| L14/N7100+ | − | 0.03 | onset of an analogy vehicle ("like a⟦ strong person⟧", "similar to⟦ a⟧", "imagine⟦ a⟧") | **HELD** under @2: 4/8 at ≥0.3, AUROC 1.00 (`03d2ef1`) |

- **+ pole: one main job with offshoots (confidence 0.45).** One computational theme, "the next token is fixed by earlier context, usually by copying a rare token sequence", explains most strong examples. It has dose-response with entropy, held-out replication of the direction, a held 8+8 test and an 8/8 causal minimal-pair result. Offshoots are fixed-phrase completions ("point of view", "each other") and predictable determiners ("handled the situation"). Against a "monosemantic" verdict: it fires on only a tiny subset of such positions, it ignores verbatim repetition, and what selects that subset is unknown.

A matched corpus regression over these features would answer it.

- **−:** use the inverse tool (DE, or the single globalMOO model) on a bank of long passages rather than short sentences, to find what actually maximises the pole. Also run the cue-deletion test with replacement words instead of deletion.

content.text:
I finished the brief: `REPORT.md` and `summary.json` are committed (last commit `0bd3636`), the working tree is clean, and it took about 75 minutes. I used no globalMOO model and skipped the SciPy inverse, because short constructed text barely moves either pole.

**Positive pole (L17/N9491+): one main job with offshoots, confidence 0.45.**
- **Label:** it fires where the next token is almost fixed by earlier context, usually the next piece of a rare name, word or code identifier already used in the document. A typical case is the "rey" in a later mention of "Dreyfus".
- **What supports it:**
  - The model's uncertainty about the next token drops steadily as activation rises, from 1.97 to 0.31 nats. The direction also held on a held-out slice of the corpus, though two of my pre-set thresholds there were missed narrowly.
  - The second 8+8 test held under the newer @2 rule, although I had predicted it would fail. It's marginal: median fire 0.224 against a 0.20 bar, and only 2 of 8 sentences reached 0.3.
  - Swapping each repeated name for a fresh one lowered activation in all 8 test passages, a 40% average drop against a 40% bar.
- **What's against it:**
  - Repeating a long chunk of text word for word does not make it fire.
  - Only about 0.035% of highly predictable tokens fire, so predictability is far from enough on its own.
  - The first label I tried, "re-mention of an earlier entity", failed 0/8.

**Negative pole (L17/N9491−): unclear or several jobs, confidence 0.25. No label survived.**
- Its strong examples often fall in the second half of a comparison, for example the decimal point in "compared to the UK's 5.1%". Contrast words appear just before about 2.3 times more often than chance.
- Both 8+8 tests failed, and the causal test rules out the comparison reading. Deleting the contrast words lowered activation slightly *less* than deleting random words (0.125 against 0.145), and half of the strong examples contain no contrast word at all.

**Feeders:** all four are weak, each removing only 3–4% of the activation, so the input is spread across many units.

| Feeder | Pole fed | Label | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| L3/N2114− | + | arsenic | held 8/8 |
| L14/N7100+ | − | start of an analogy ("like a…") | held |
| L9/N1314+ | − | vampires | failed, but two of my "near misses" were really vampire-fiction names, so the test was flawed |
| L15/N8076+ | + | pieces of code identifiers | failed 0/8 |

All four edges are recorded.

**Process notes:**
- I withdrew one pre-registration (`84843ff`). The test runner reads `<` characters in code as unfilled placeholders, so I re-registered it as `9e322f7` with the comparisons written as `>` instead. The report records this.
- Every pre-registration commit hash is listed in the report.
- The exploration outputs, blind-labelling samples and analysis scripts are in `notes/`.
